title: EU Officials: ‘Britain Will Have to Pay a Price’ for Brexit
main_content:
Britain will have to pay a price, if it exits the European Union — if for no other reason than to send a warning message to other member countries that may consider leaving the bloc.

In the run-up to Britain’s June 23 referendum, Brussels officials and European lawmakers are warning London it will face tough — if not harsh — negotiations to conclude a post-Brexit free trade deal like Norway’s or Switzerland’s with the EU.

questions.question: Why will Britain have to pay a price if it exits the EU?
options: To send a warning message to other member countries that may consider leaving the bloc.
To improve its economic standing independently.
To negotiate better trade deals with the US.
questions.answer: To send a warning message to other member countries that may consider leaving the bloc.

questions.question: What are Brussels officials and European lawmakers warning London about?
options: It will face tough, if not harsh, negotiations for a post-Brexit free trade deal.
It will automatically receive a Norway-style trade deal.
It will be excluded from all future trade with the EU.
It will be able to negotiate without any conditions.
questions.answer: It will face tough, if not harsh, negotiations for a post-Brexit free trade deal.
